records.name: Applied Mechanics
records.summary: A Philadelphia theater company that builds original immersive plays about social change with its performers and director. It also teaches workshops for theater makers and runs sessions for teams.
records.what_you_do: Performers and a director build original plays for live audiences. You can buy tickets to a show, take one of the company's workshops, or sign up for the mailing list to hear about new productions.

schedule.text: Productions run for set dates, announced on the company's site. The pages we checked did not list showtimes, so check the ticket page before you plan a trip.

locations.label: Christ Church Neighborhood House (venue for Run Ben Run)

cost.text: Ticket prices are not listed on the pages we checked. Tickets are sold through Ticketleap.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to Run Ben Run through the Ticketleap link on the home page, or sign up for the mailing list on the Contact page.
first_step.basis: Shows are open to the public and tickets are sold online. The workshops page lists classes that suit theater people, but it gives no date for the next one and no way to join the company itself.
first_step.what_to_expect: A visit is a live staged play performed by the company's performers and directed by its director. The current show is a satire built around the painting American Progress. The pages we checked did not give the running time or the price, so confirm both on the ticket page.
first_visit_tips: Buy tickets ahead on Ticketleap, since the pages we checked do not say whether tickets are sold at the door.
Read the digital program on the Run Ben Run page before the show. It covers the painting behind the play.
Email appmechsinfo@gmail.com with access questions, since the site lists no accessibility details.

records.notes: Workshops page: the only dated workshop item is January 2026 registration, which has passed; no later workshop dates were found. Accessibility is not stated on any page checked. The venue address is not on the site.

records.name: ArcheDream for Humankind
records.summary: A touring blacklight mask and dance theater company, founded in 2001, that makes shows for all ages, teaches workshops, and runs a summer camp with scholarships.
records.what_you_do: See a public show such as WEIRDOFEST, book a performance or workshop through the contact form, or support the MoveMakers summer camp scholarships.

schedule.text: The company tours, so shows and workshops are booked directly with it, and upcoming dates are posted on its site. The MoveMakers summer camp offers scholarships each summer.

cost.text: Ticket and workshop prices are not listed on the site. Ask through the contact form or by phone.

first_step.how: Go to the public show WEIRDOFEST at Philadelphia Brewing (the site lists October 17, 2 to 10 pm, without the year), or send a question through the contact form about a workshop or the MoveMakers camp.
first_step.basis: Shows are public and the contact form is open to anyone. The site has no class sign up or membership steps, so the way in is to attend a show or ask about a workshop.
first_step.what_to_expect: A show is a blacklight performance that mixes masks, puppetry, storytelling, and music, and the company describes its shows as suitable for audiences of all ages. The site does not list ticket prices, running times, or seating, so ask before you go. Workshops are booked by request.
first_visit_tips: Call 610-574-6037 or use the contact form to ask about tickets and timing.
The site does not print the year for WEIRDOFEST, so confirm the date before you go.
The site says shows are for all ages, but ask about the running time before bringing very young children.

records.notes: Single-page site: every menu item (Home, About, MoveMakers, Videos, Contact) points to the same address, so no separate camp, join, or workshop page exists to read. One web search for the MoveMakers camp found no pages from this group, so camp dates, cost, and scholarship terms are unverified and nothing from unrelated camps was used. WEIRDOFEST is listed for October 17 with no year. The Say Yes Philly fundraiser is dated 2026 with no month, so last_sign_of_life is left empty.

records.name: Ars Nova Workshop
records.summary: A nonprofit that presents live new jazz and improvised music in Philadelphia, mostly at the Solar Myth venue. It also runs a mentoring series, a podcast, and a membership program.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to a listed show, join the mailing list for news, become a member for ticket discounts, or sign up on the Volunteer page to help at events.

schedule.text: Concerts are held most months at Solar Myth, usually at 8 pm. Buy tickets for a listed show through its ticket link.

cost.text: Tickets are sold per show, and prices are not listed on the pages we checked. Membership is billed monthly, from $10 a month to $150 a month, and includes ticket discounts.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to an upcoming show through the ticket link on the What's On page, or join the mailing list first to hear about new dates.
first_step.basis: Concerts are sold to anyone through ticket links, and the volunteer form is open to the public. The site has no beginner program, so this is about attending shows rather than learning a skill.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most shows are evening concerts at Solar Myth, usually starting at 8 pm. Tickets are bought through linked ticketing pages, and some shows sell out, so buy early. Members get early access and discounts if you plan to come often.
first_visit_tips: Plan for an evening start, since most listed shows begin at 8 pm.
Buy tickets ahead through the ticket link, since some shows sell out.
If you want to help at events, use the online volunteer form; it places you in a pool of volunteers.

records.notes: Membership tiers, billed monthly: Mars $10, Venus $20, Jupiter $40, Saturn $150. The membership page does not say whether non-members can attend concerts. The programs page is mostly past festivals and exhibitions from 2019 to 2025, plus a Coltrane 100 series running September 2026 to September 2027. The volunteer page is a form with no email or phone, and roles are occasional (mailings, event staffing). The Jazz Gallery Mentoring Series is named as a partner; see leads_only.

records.name: Artcinia LLC
records.summary: A small arts presenter that runs a Music in Your Neighborhood program, bringing professional local musicians to neighborhood venues. The site lists no upcoming shows, and its newest dated item is from October 2022.
records.what_you_do: Ask about becoming an Artcinia Ambassador through the contact form, or join the mailing list to hear about future concerts.

cost.text: Concert prices are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Use the contact form on artcinia.com to ask about the Ambassador role, and tick the box to join the email list.
first_step.basis: The email list and the Ambassador invitation are open to anyone, but the site does not describe the role and lists no shows, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site describes neighborhood concerts by local professional musicians. It does not show any recent or upcoming shows, times, or venues, so a first visit cannot be planned from the site alone. Contact the company first to ask what is coming up.
first_visit_tips: Use the contact form, since the site lists no email address or phone number.
Expect no set schedule; the concerts page shows no upcoming shows at this check.

records.notes: The concerts page has empty Upcoming and Past headings. The only dated item is a reader testimonial about an October 2022 neighborhood concert in South Philadelphia, which sets the status at dormant. Photo file names with 2023 dates were not treated as evidence. Verdict left at publish because the group is not known to be closed and the site invites Ambassadors. The reviewer may prefer to hide it as dormant.

records.name: Arthur Ross Gallery
records.summary: A free art gallery at the University of Pennsylvania that shows exhibitions and hosts artist talks, lectures, and guided tours, all open to the public.
records.what_you_do: Visit the gallery for free during open hours, come to an artist talk or lecture, request a guided tour, or give at a Friends level, which starts at $100.

schedule.text: Open seven days a week. The site footer lists Monday to Thursday 11 am to 6 pm and Friday to Sunday noon to 5 pm, but the Plan Your Visit page lists different hours, so call 215.898.2083 to confirm before you go.

locations.label: Gallery in Fisher Fine Arts Library

cost.text: Admission is free and open to the public. Friends gifts start at $100.

access.notes: Fully wheelchair-accessible entrance on the south side of the Fisher Fine Arts Library at 232 S. 34th Street. Call the front desk at 215.898.1479 on arrival and staff will come down to meet you. Large-print wall labels and low-vision tours are available on request.

first_step.how: Walk in during open hours, or call 215-898-2083 to request a guided tour.
first_step.basis: Free and open to the public, with posted hours, talks, and guided tours for all ages that you can request by phone. The site names no newcomer program.
first_step.what_to_expect: A visit is a walk through free exhibitions in the historic Frank Furness building, where the gallery sits inside the Fisher Fine Arts Library. Talks are led by artists or curators, and tours are led by gallery staff, interns, or student guides. Check the posted hours before you come, because the site lists two different sets.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-898-2083 to confirm the hours before you visit.
Park in a campus garage. The site names Chestnut 34 at 3335 Chestnut St as the closest option.
If you use a wheelchair, enter at the south side at 232 S. 34th Street and call the front desk when you arrive.

records.notes: Hours conflict: the footer shows Monday to Thursday 11 to 6 and Friday to Sunday noon to 5, while Plan Your Visit shows Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday 10 to 5, Wednesday 11 to 6, and Saturday and Sunday noon to 5. Both are recorded in schedule text. Upcoming 2026 items on the events page: artist talks on Oct 9 and Oct 22 (no times), a lecture on Nov 11, a curators conversation on Nov 14, Yoga in the Gallery from Sept 23 to Nov 18, a film screening on Dec 6, and student-guided tours from Aug 29 to Dec 13. None of these list times or registration details. Friends levels: Young Friend $100, Supporter $500, Patron $1,000.

records.name: Artístas y Músicos Latino Americanos
records.summary: A music group that teaches Latin American and Puerto Rican music to children and adults. Offerings include guitar, cuatro, and percussion classes, private and group lessons, an after-school program, and a Latin Music Clubhouse.
records.what_you_do: Book private or group lessons on an instrument, take a class such as youth guitar, Puerto Rican cuatro, or Latin percussion, or join the after-school program. After-school classes are free for enrolled Esperanza Academy students.

schedule.text: Private lessons meet Tuesdays and Thursdays from 4:30 to 8 pm, with the exact time set by teacher and studio availability. After-school music classes for Esperanza Academy students meet on weekday afternoons during the school year.

cost.text: Private lessons are billed every four weeks for four lessons. 30 minutes is $160 for adults and $120 for youth, 45 minutes is $240 and $180, and 60 minutes is $320 and $240. A registration fee is also charged, and its amount is not on the page. Automatic payment is preferred, and you can cancel with four weeks' notice. After-school programs are free for enrolled Esperanza Academy students.

first_step.how: Fill out the online registration form at amla.org, choosing an instrument, lesson day, and lesson length, then book the required 30-minute orientation.
first_step.basis: Anyone can register for private or group lessons, including adult beginners, and the 30-minute orientation comes before any payment. Youth after-school spots are for enrolled Esperanza Academy students, and final group class registration closed October 3, 2026.
first_step.what_to_expect: Expect private or group lessons at the music studios inside Esperanza, usually on Tuesdays or Thursdays between 4:30 and 8 pm. Lessons can cover technique, reading music, ear training, and performance, in Latin American traditions as well as classical, jazz, and pop. Start with the orientation, then pay the registration fee and the first four weeks of lessons.
first_visit_tips: Use Esperanza's main doors on Bristol Street near 5th Street. The site gives two floor levels for the music space, so confirm when you book.
Book the orientation before you pay, so you can see what the lessons are like first.
Pick your lesson length carefully, since 30, 45, and 60 minute lessons are priced differently.

records.notes: After-school classes are for enrolled Esperanza Academy students (elementary, middle, and high school strands). Calendar dates for 2026 to 2027: registration Aug 3 to Sept 4, 2026; final group class registration Sept 28 to Oct 3, 2026; group classes begin Oct 7, 2026. The contact page names Daniel de Jesus as the person to ask about classes; the tier 1 contact name Matt Lentz is kept because it is not disproved. The calendar's MLK Day (Jan 19, 2027) and Presidents Day (Feb 16, 2027) fall on Tuesdays, which does not match the usual Monday observances, so confirm with AMLA. The programs page also lists a summer 2026 anti-violence songwriting program, in-school residencies, and a booking service; these are not part of the record. Footer copyright lines read 2021 and were not used as evidence.

records.name: ArtPhilly
records.summary: A Philadelphia arts group of creators across many art forms that puts on a citywide arts festival with projects in venues around the city.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to a festival project, browse the project list, or sign up for the newsletter to hear about the next festival.

schedule.text: The group runs a citywide arts festival as a season of projects, not weekly classes. The pages checked do not give dates for a next festival.

cost.text: Many festival events are free, and some free events need an RSVP. Ticketed events are $26 standard, or $13 for students, children, seniors, and arts and industry workers, and $2 for EBT card holders. All ticket sales are final, and cancelled shows get full refunds.

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter at artphilly.org and follow the group's Instagram, then pick a project from the next festival's list when it posts.
first_step.basis: Festival events are open to the public and tickets are sold online, but the site shows no class, membership, or volunteer path, and no festival is running now, so the newsletter is the only way in.
first_step.what_to_expect: A visit is one festival project, which can range from theater and music to dinners and events in parks, museums, and theaters. Standard tickets are $26, and some events are free. Each project lists its own venue and time, so check the project page before you go.
first_visit_tips: All ticket sales are final, so check the date and venue before you buy.
Door sales are first come, first served, and some shows sell out, so buy ahead if you can.
Write to info@artphilly.org about date changes, since changes are not guaranteed.

records.notes: The FAQ says the What Now 2026 festival ran May 27 to July 2, 2026, but the home page still describes it as current. Treat the festival as over; no dates for a next festival were found. The contact page and events page returned 404 at check time, so the email comes from the FAQ (info@artphilly.org). The tier 1 email hannah@almacommunications.co is not on any page checked and was replaced; the reviewer may restore it if it is the right contact. The FAQ's accessibility link has no readable text, so accessibility is not recorded. Festival projects were held at many venues, so no single location is listed. Online_ok is set to true because at least one 2026 festival project was listed as online.
